title: Arun Govil Returns to the Ramayana as King Dashrath
excerpt: The makers of Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic unveiled a first-look poster of Govil as the King of Ayodhya, 39 years after he immortalised Lord Ram on television.
body:
• The makers of Ramayana unveiled a first-look solo poster of Arun Govil as King Dashrath, the King of Ayodhya and father of Lord Ram, in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic.
  • Govil is inseparable from the role of Lord Ram, which he played in Ramanand Sagar's 1987 television series Ramayan. He now steps into the role of the father of the character that defined his career.
  • The poster shows Govil in elaborate royal regalia, seated on a throne, with the caption: “He once brought Ram to life for a generation. Now, he returns to the world of Ramayana as the King of Ayodhya.”
  • Ramayana: Part 1 releases worldwide on November 5, 2026 — just in time for Diwali — in five Indian languages plus IMAX, with Sony Pictures distributing internationally. Part 2 follows at Diwali 2027.

The makers of Ramayana have unveiled a new solo poster featuring Arun Govil as King Dashrath, giving audiences their first look at the veteran actor in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part cinematic epic. In the poster, Govil appears in a regal avatar — elaborate royal regalia befitting the King of Ayodhya, seated on a throne with an unmistakable air of authority.

The poster was shared on social media with a caption that leans fully into the casting's resonance: “He once brought Ram to life for a generation. Now, he returns to the world of Ramayana as the King of Ayodhya. Arun Govil as King Dashrath.”

The reveal is the latest character introduction for a project already among the most ambitious Indian films in production. It also sets up a striking on-screen dynamic: Govil, forever associated with playing Lord Ram, will now play Ram's father in a film where Ranbir Kapoor takes on the role of Lord Ram himself.

Context & Background

Arun Govil's association with the Ramayana story goes back nearly four decades. He played Lord Ram in Ramanand Sagar's 1987 television series Ramayan, a portrayal that became an enduring part of his career and public identity across generations of Indian viewers. Filmfare noted the qualities that set that performance's standard — calm demeanour, poised stature and a soothing smile — and argued that watching him take on the role of the father establishes a deeper connection “between the actor, the fans, and the epic in itself.”

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1zip1rNaNYs https://x.com/DharmaMovies/status/2107722724034683054

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is being mounted as a two-part epic with an ensemble led by Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Rocking Star Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, the eight-time Oscar-winning DNEG handling visual effects and A.R. Rahman scoring alongside Hans Zimmer.

The film will release across India in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, and in IMAX. Sony Pictures handles global distribution outside India; Dharma Productions distributes in the Hindi-speaking market. Part 1 is scheduled worldwide for November 5, 2026, with Part 2 at Diwali 2027.

Impact & Analysis

This casting choice converts four decades of audience memory into box-office equity. Govil is not a nostalgic cameo — he is stepping into a central figure in Rama's family story, the king whose decisions set the epic's central tragedy in motion. The poster campaign is clearly built around the faces of this ensemble, and Govil's carries the deepest resonance for viewers who grew up with the television series.

There is a narrative layer to it as well. Dashrath is the father who, bound by a promise, sends his son into exile. Having the actor who embodied Ram's virtue for a generation play the father forced to make that call adds dramatic weight — a different interpretation of Govil's connection to the epic, moving from the iconic Lord Ram of Indian television to the king who sends him away.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, this casting lands with unusual force. The 1987 Ramayan was appointment television in Indian households across the world — families in the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf organized their Sunday mornings around it. Govil's Ram is, for millions abroad, the visual memory of the epic itself, passed down through rewatches and stories told to children born outside India.

The November 5, 2026 worldwide release — with Sony Pictures distributing internationally — means diaspora audiences get the film at the same moment as Indian viewers, timed to the Diwali season when cultural connection is at its peak. Govil's return gives older generations a reason to be in the theatre alongside younger ones who know him only through their parents' memories.

“He once brought Ram to life for a generation. Now, he returns to the world of Ramayana as the King of Ayodhya. Arun Govil as King Dashrath.”

— The makers of Ramayana, via the film's social media accounts

What's Next

The poster marks the start of the film's character-reveal campaign, and more solo posters from the ensemble are expected in the coming weeks — attention will turn to first looks at Ranbir Kapoor's Ram, Sai Pallavi's Sita and Yash's Ravana. With Part 1 locked for a worldwide release on November 5, 2026, a trailer is the obvious next milestone as the film's marketing builds toward the Diwali corridor.

The bigger question the poster campaign is already answering: whether a two-part retelling of India's most-told story can justify its scale. The casting so far — legacy and stardom in the same frame — suggests the producers intend to. The proof arrives in theatres just over a year from now.
